stem:
The given figure shows the pathway of a nerve impulse in a reflex action. Which part serves as a link between neurons?

(The figure is a reflex-arc diagram: a hand near a hot vessel, with the impulse pathway drawn up to a cross-section of the spinal cord and back to the arm muscle. Four points along the pathway are labelled — X on the incoming sensory limb, Y a loop near the hand, W on the outgoing motor limb to the muscle, and Z pointing into the grey matter inside the spinal cord.)

The given graph shows changes in the air pressure of lungs during breathing. What causes the change in air pressure during period X?

(The figure is a graph of "Air pressure in the lungs (kPa)" on the vertical axis against "Time" on the horizontal axis. During the interval marked X at the start, the trace falls to a trough — the lung air pressure decreases — before rising again to a peak.)

options.label: A
options.text: Movement of ribs downward and inward

options.label: C
options.text: Relaxation of the external intercostal muscles

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease in the volume of the lungs

stem:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the given figure?

1. The parts labelled as Q and R carry blood having low oxygen concentration.
2. The parts labelled as P, Q and R carry blood having low oxygen concentration.
3. The blood flows out of the heart through blood vessel Q when ventricle contracts.
4. The blood is flowing out of the heart through blood vessel Q when atria contract.

(The figure is an external view of the human heart with three great vessels labelled: P points to the aorta arching off the top, R points to a vena cava on the upper-left entering the right atrium, and Q points to the pulmonary artery leaving the right ventricle.)

A well-stained leaf peel preparation when focused under the high power of the microscope would show:

1. epidermal cells, stomata, guard cells each with one nucleus and many chloroplasts
2. epidermal cells, stomata, guard cells with many nuclei and one chloroplast each
3. stomata and guard cells without nuclei or chloroplast
4. stomata but no guard cells or epidermal cells

Refer to the given figure of heart and select the correct statement.

(The figure is an internal cut-away of the human heart showing all four chambers. The two upper chambers (atria) are labelled X on the left of the view and Y on the right; the two lower chambers (ventricles) are labelled P below X and Q below Y. In this anterior view X/P are the right atrium and right ventricle, and Y/Q are the left atrium and left ventricle.)

options.label: A
options.text: Q receives deoxygenated blood from Y.

options.label: C
options.text: The blood from Y reaches lungs.

options.label: D
options.text: The blood from body enters heart through P.

stem:
Refer to the following figure of phloem tissue. Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between cells Y and Z?

(The figure is a longitudinal diagram of phloem tissue showing vertical files of cells with stippled horizontal sieve plates. Y points to a narrow cell beside the conducting file, and Z points to the broad sieve-tube element bearing the sieve plates — i.e. Y is the companion cell and Z is the sieve-tube member, which lacks a nucleus at maturity.)

options.label: A
options.text: Y contains ribosomes that synthesise proteins required by Z.

options.label: B
options.text: Y provides the carbohydrates that are transported by Z.

options.label: C
options.text: Y transports sucrose, while Z transports water and minerals.

options.label: D
options.text: Y helps to filter the liquid transported in Z to facilitate translocation.
